ideas.title: Glass rain, lit
ideas.critique: The step is real but small: spots that were painted become emitters, and the film is still friends chasing sun spots on the meadow, so a viewer sees the same short again with better light. This would be the fourth light-on-the-meadow post running. The bellies lit from below by moving lights is the only new thing to watch, and it has to come through clearly in the trace or the step disappears.

ideas.title: Statues in the lighthouse beam
ideas.critique: Most people already know this children's game, and the idea is a rule set wrapped around one rotating light, so the premise is predictable. What is strong is that it can be played: the light becomes a rule the player has to dodge, and creatures caught mid-step freezing in a beam that sweeps through the trace is a picture with tension in it.

ideas.title: The sea goes out
ideas.critique: This changes the whole island's water again, like the seesaw flood and the drift, and the payoff is a scripted race back from the wave. Stranded fish and shells are set dressing. Nothing in it moves in a new way unless the returning wave is a real simulation, and the pitch does not promise one.

ideas.title: Hat thief
ideas.critique: A crab stealing things is a cartoon gag you would expect. The wobbling physical tower and hats raining down when it falls do give the island a new way for things to move and a mess worth watching twice. It stands or falls on the sway and the topple looking weighty, not on the snipping.

ideas.title: Your own raincloud
ideas.critique: A personal raincloud is a stock cartoon image, and in the end this is tag with a different marker, a roaming effect handed between creatures. The puddles left behind are the one thing that stays and could be read afterwards, but as pitched they are a footnote.

ideas.title: Bubble-wrap meadow
ideas.critique: Turning the ground into a new material that reacts to steps is the recipe of the sand rule. What is fresh is sound, which the island has barely used, and a pop chain racing across the meadow could be satisfying. Without real per-bubble deformation it is a texture swap plus a sound effect.

ideas.title: Lumi throws a tantrum
ideas.critique: A fourth close-up set-piece gag centred on Lumi, and a tantrum is the first thing anyone would picture for a bored character. Driving it from the real boredom value and having nearby props jump with each kick is honest work on Lumi's body. The friends standing and staring will look like the earlier non-reactions unless they actually respond.

ideas.title: Snow globe
ideas.critique: Putting the island under glass is a familiar picture, and it encloses the island without adding anything to play with. The strong parts are a giant refracting dome bending the island from outside, which a raster engine cannot do, and a particle system that swirls up and settles when someone jumps. If the glitter does not settle physically, it is a prop with a shader.

ideas.title: The pond lags behind
ideas.critique: Showing the world's own past back to it is the TV post's trick (the previous frame on a screen), moved into a pond. The strong part is the creatures noticing and testing their late selves, which the TV never had. That reaction is the whole payoff, and it will be scripted unless it grows out of what they really did.

ideas.title: Everyone's footprints glow
ideas.critique: Turning a walk into a trace is close to the domino line that Lumi's walk laid, and it is one more night-light post. Real movement logged as fading light that you can read at night is a good use of moving emitters, but once you have read the map there is little to watch a second time.
